finding.title: Give sync_status_emission_test.dart's 'empty outbox + online + after pull → synced' test actual assertions

evidence.quote: test('empty outbox + online + after pull → synced', () async {
// No assertion here — pre-pull, status remains whatever the failed

finding.why: The test's name and the file's own header matrix both promise to verify the 'synced' cell (empty outbox + online + a completed pull), but the body ends after recordDrainAttempt() with a comment admitting no assertion is made, because _EmptyGateway cannot simulate a successful pull (every real fetch throws via noSuchMethod). The test always passes regardless of whether synced emission is broken for this exact scenario — it is pure green-checkmark noise. SyncStatusSynced IS exercised elsewhere in the same file, but only via the throttled-resume branch (_everPulledOnLaunch force-set by the throttle, not by a genuinely completed pull), so the 'real successful cold pull → synced' path this test is named for has no working assertion anywhere in the file.
finding.recommendation: Either delete the test, or give it a gateway fake that lets pullOnLaunch complete successfully (mirroring _ProfileProgramsGateway in sync_rework_profile_programs_pull_test.dart) and assert `orchestrator.currentStatus is SyncStatusSynced` afterward.
acceptance_criteria: the 'empty outbox + online + after pull → synced' test contains at least one expect() against SyncStatus, or is removed
if kept, the pull it drives completes successfully (non-throttled) before the synced assertion

finding.title: Log SchedulerStageRepositoryImpl's schedule-JSON decode failure instead of silently swallowing it
finding.why: If a stage's schedule JSON column is ever malformed (migration bug, manual DB edit, a bad sync-merge write), every read of that stage silently substitutes a hardcoded delay_days:0 default with zero AppLogger call — changing that stage's chazara/review timing with no diagnostic trail to explain a future 'my review schedule looks wrong' report. SchedulerStageRepositoryImpl also has no dedicated unit test file (grep across test/ confirms it is only exercised indirectly, with well-formed data, through SchedulerEngine/DailyTaskGenerator integration tests), so this fallback path is completely unexercised by the suite.
finding.recommendation: Log via AppLogger (including the row id and raw schedule string) in the catch before falling back, and add a unit test for the fallback path.
acceptance_criteria: The catch in _rowToSchedulerStage calls AppLogger.warning/error with the stage row id and raw schedule string before falling back to the default.
New unit test constructs a StageDefinition row with malformed schedule JSON and asserts both the fallback SchedulerStage values and that the log call fired.

finding.title: Fix the self-referential SY-3 timeout-message assertion in sync_orchestrator_test.dart — it never calls SyncOrchestratorImpl

evidence.quote:
const message = 'Sync timed out — tap to retry';
      expect(message, contains('timed out'));

finding.why: The test declares its own local `message` string literal and asserts it contains 'timed out' — guaranteed true by the literal it just wrote — then compares a bare TimeoutException.toString() against that same local constant. It never touches SyncOrchestratorImpl or its catch block, so it provides zero protection for the orchestrator's actual TimeoutException-handling path. A maintainer reading this file alone would believe SY-3's friendly-timeout-message behavior is covered right here. Genuine end-to-end coverage of the same behavior does exist, but in a different file (test/sync/sy3_sync_error_message_sanitize_test.dart, outside this batch) — this copy is dead weight that would mask a real gap if that sibling file were ever trimmed or moved.
finding.recommendation: Delete this test (real coverage lives in test/sync/sy3_sync_error_message_sanitize_test.dart) or rewrite it to call orchestrator.pullOnLaunch() with a TimeoutException-throwing fake gateway and assert on the emitted SyncStatusError.message, matching the pattern used two tests above it in this same file.
acceptance_criteria: Test either removed with the reason in the commit message (TQ-7) or rewritten to drive pullOnLaunch() through a timeout-throwing fake gateway and assert the resulting SyncStatusError.message

finding.title: Pin StreakStateProvider's day-bucketing seam instead of letting streak_state_provider_test.dart depend on the host machine's timezone
finding.why: read()/watch() call StreakReducer.reduce() without pinning the injectable `dayOf` seam that streak_reducer.dart's own doc comment says exists precisely 'so tests can pin a fixed UTC offset deterministically without depending on the host machine's timezone.' Both FakeLocalDayClock.today() and the default dayOf (DateUtils.extractLocalDate, date_utils.dart:64) resolve through DateTime.toLocal(), which reads the executing machine's TZ -- confirmed empirically inside the real flutter_tester harness: `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati flutter test` shows DateTime.utc(2026,5,14,12).toLocal() shift a full calendar day. I could not flip any assertion in this specific file under that TZ (ran the suite 3x under the sandbox default Europe/London and once under forced Pacific/Kiritimati, all 13 tests green each time) because every fixture here sits at hour 0 or hour 12 UTC and every current day-gap still lands inside the reducer's +/-1-day grace window either way -- that is a property of today's specific fixture values, not a guarantee. The sibling unit suite (test/features/sync/domain/reducers/streak_reducer_test.dart:120-158) already tests the local-vs-UTC distinction correctly by injecting dayOf directly; this integration-level file has no such seam and inherits toLocal()'s host dependency instead. A fixture pair whose UTC-hour asymmetry straddles a day boundary differently under some real TZ (e.g. clock seeded at 23:00 UTC, event at 01:00 UTC) would confirm an actual flip -- the D17 rollover test already seeds close to a boundary and is the most likely one to trip this by accident in a future edit.
finding.recommendation: Either give StreakStateProvider.read/watch an explicit dayOf override (mirroring the reducer's own seam) or have the test suite pin TZ=UTC explicitly (Makefile/CI env var) so pass/fail can't depend on the runner's locale.
acceptance_criteria: `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati flutter test test/core/streak/streak_state_provider_test.dart` and the default-TZ run both stay green by construction (pinned dayOf or pinned TZ), not by coincidence of current fixture values.

finding.title: Fix SefariaRef.titlePart/addressPart to match the documented chapter:verse split (or fix the docs)
finding.rule: Evans (ubiquitous-language contract) / TQ-7-TQ-8 spirit (test encodes the bug instead of catching it)
finding.why: The class docstring's own worked example says titlePart of "Mishnah Berakhot 1:1" is "Mishnah Berakhot" (address "1:1"). The `_splitTail` regex only strips a single trailing digit run (optionally +1 letter), so it can never cross the ':' in a chapter:verse address — for that exact documented example it actually produces titlePart == "Mishnah Berakhot 1:" and addressPart == "1". The test file's own inline comment ('let's assert what we actually produce... The SefariaRef titlePart splits on the LAST pure-numeric token') shows the author noticed the mismatch and wrote the test to lock in the wrong output rather than fix the regex or the docs. Mishnah/Tanach chapter:verse is the single most common ref shape in this Torah-study app, so any future caller of titlePart/addressPart (currently unused in production) inherits silently wrong output for the primary case, with a green regression test giving false confidence.
finding.recommendation: Either extend `_splitTail` to also recognize a `\d+:\d+` chapter:verse tail as one address token, or correct the docstring to describe the actual single-digit-run behavior — then update the test to assert the corrected contract, not the current output.
acceptance_criteria: SefariaRef.parse('Mishnah Berakhot 1:1').titlePart equals whatever the corrected docstring promises (either 'Mishnah Berakhot' with the regex fixed, or the docstring rewritten to match current behavior).
sefaria_ref_test.dart's titlePart test for chapter:verse refs no longer contains a comment acknowledging the assertion doesn't match the documented contract.
